description: An EXTENDED LETTER as a character of a COBOL word — ISO §2023:8.3.2.1: "Each character of a COBOL word … shall be selected from the set of basic letters, basic digits, extended letters, and the basic special characters hyphen and underscore", with §2023:8.1.3.2 GR4 making the extended letters the Annex B repertoire less the basic characters (Annex A.4.6, claimed). A COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): §1985:IV.4.2.2.1: 'Each character of a COBOL word that is not a special character word is selected from the set of letters, digits, and the hyphen; the hyphen may not appear as the first or last character in such words', and §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.1: 'Each character of a user-defined word is selected from the set of characters 'A', 'B', 'C', ... , 'Z', '0', ... , '9', and '-''; §2002:8.3.1.1: 'Each character of a COBOL word that is not a special character word shall be selected from the set of basic letters, basic digits, extended letters, and the basic special characters hyphen and underscore. The hyphen or underscore shall not appear as the first or last character in such words.' §2002:8.1.2.1 GR4: 'The set of extended letters consists of characters from the repertoire specified in Annex C, Characters permitted in user-defined words', and §2002:F.2 item 81 states the change: 'User-defined words may contain extended letters.' §2014:8.3.1.1 keeps the sentence and §2014:8.1.2.1 GR4 the set (its Annex B), so 2014 = 2023 for the gate; the repertoire itself then changed 2014->2023 per §2023:E.2 item 4 and E.3.3 items 4/5 (VCR row 10, CobolCharacterRepertoire). Lexed at EVERY edition (superset-lex / bind-narrow) so the below-2002 rejection is this named gate rather than a lexical error; from 2002 the Annex B position rules are COBOL2773. kb/Work PB1402.
display: an extended letter in a COBOL word
